translation:
The black orb belongs to the liver, and the liver is wood. The east belongs to wood, and wood generates wind. In the viscera it is the liver, responding in the eye. When violent anger is frequent, internal stagnation arises, and moreover wind-heat invades the pupil with films. Its syndrome arises from frequent anger and rage, excess of toil and labor, external contraction of wind-cold, and internal injury from lust, so that the head and eyes become dizzy and things are not seen clearly; if it is not treated for a long time, it finally becomes dimness and darkness and similar syndromes.

The inner and outer canthi belong to the heart, and the heart is fire. The heart dwells in the pericardium and is named the sovereign. The blood pursues the fire and rushes to congeal within the eye. By the largeness or smallness of the canthal heads one distinguishes deficiency and excess; even distant vision is likewise a fire star. Its syndrome arises from worry and sorrow, vexation and toil, grief and bitter brooding, which injure the heart within and attack the eye without, so that red sinews pour into the pupil and fleshy growths climb over the eye; if it is not treated for a long time, it gradually reaches blindness and similar syndromes.

The upper and lower eyelids belong to the spleen, and the spleen is earth. The sun belongs to earth and governs the spleen's origin. When accumulated heat interferes, the disease has its source. The upper and lower eyelids swell and are red, and styes break out from time to time, their roots remaining. Its syndrome arises from eating much hot food, roasted and grilled things, and pungent and sour things, so that congested heat is within, stagnant blood swells and pains, and millet-like grains cause hidden irritation; if it is not treated for a long time, it finally reaches ulcerated lid margins and inverted lashes, lingering without end, and similar syndromes.

The white orb belongs to the lungs, and the lungs are metal. When the lung viscus retains and the heart-heat attacks, both eyes faintly appear as if wrapped in crimson gauze. Only by dispersing and freeing the intestines and stomach with pungent-cool agents can one resolve the dimness that is red like fire. Its syndrome arises from braving frost and snow, irregularity of hunger and satiety, receiving wind pathogen without, and internal heat attacking upward; if it is not treated for a long time, it finally causes things to be seen unclearly, a white membrane covering the eye, pain making it hard to open, and tears flowing when facing the wind, and similar syndromes.

The pupil belongs to the kidneys, and the kidneys are water. It also communicates with the orifice of the gallbladder. Here water and wood have the meaning of mutual generation, and the liver and kidneys have formulas for joint treatment. When the kidneys and gallbladder share the same source, the essence naturally flourishes; when yin is deficient and fire is exuberant, flowers are then produced. When it rushes upward against the spirit water, it becomes green; urgently nourish the source of transformation and do not sigh. Its syndrome arises from insatiable desires, excess of sexual indulgence, great fright injuring the spirit, and great fear injuring the will. When water and fire are already deficient and yin and yang gradually damaged, cold tears flow down the face, flying flowers pass before the eyes, green water pours into the pupil, and green blindness and internal cataracts and similar syndromes arise.
translator_notes: 挑針 (tiaozhen) refers to a stye (hordeolum).
爛弦 (lanxian) is ulceration of the lid margin; 倒睫 (daojie) is trichiasis.
胬肉攀睛 (nurou panjing) is a pterygium covering the eye.
飛花 (feihua) refers to the symptom of flowers flying before the eyes, i.e., floaters.
